text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "logistics/access.py already defines the status codes OPEN, RESTRICTED, CLOSED = \"A\", \"R\", \"X\" and STATUS_CODES = (OPEN, RESTRICTED, CLOSED), plus VEHICLE_WEIGHT = {\"truck\": \"heavy\", \"van\": \"light\"}. The docstring says: A = open to all vehicles, R = restricted (closed to all vehicles until cleared), X = closed to all vehicles. can_pass must interpret these codes; note the docstring gives no per-vehicle distinction, so both R and X block both vehicles as written.", "file": "logistics/access.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "logistics/access.py provides road_status(road_id: str, network: dict | None = None) -> str, which raises KeyError for an unknown road and ValueError for an unknown status code; it defaults network to load_network(). can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network=None) can reuse this. load_network() -> dict reads store.read_json(\"network.json\").", "file": "logistics/access.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "logistics/routes.py defines CAPACITY = {\"truck\": 40, \"van\": 12} and DEFAULT_VEHICLE = \"truck\". best_route(warehouse_id, site, network=None) returns (min(options, key=lambda r: (r['km'], r['id'])), DEFAULT_VEHICLE) or None if routes_between finds no route with r['from'] == warehouse_id and r['to'] == site. Ties on km are broken by route id.", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "Routes in data/network.json are fixed lists of roads: each route dict has keys id, from, to, roads (list of road ids like \"R-01\"), and km. passable_route can iterate network['routes'] filtered by from/to (routes_between does exactly this) and check every road id in r['roads'].", "file": "data/network.json"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "Current network data: R-03, R-09, R-13 have status \"R\"; R-08 and R-12 have status \"X\"; all others \"A\". Affected routes: RT-02 (WH-NVL-03->SITE-NVL-B, 22km, uses R-03), RT-05 (WH-CPL-05->SITE-CPL-B, 18km, uses R-08), RT-07 (WH-HGL-07->SITE-HGL-A, 20km, uses R-12), RT-09 (WH-HGL-07->SITE-HGL-B, 35km, uses R-13). Fallbacks exist: RT-03 (31km) for SITE-NVL-B, RT-06 (26km) for SITE-CPL-B, RT-08 (27km) for SITE-HGL-A; SITE-HGL-B has no alternative route.", "file": "data/network.json"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "notifications/sms.py has TEMPLATES with key \"DELIVERY_MOVED\": \"Lifeline: road closures. Your aid will now be at {site} on {day}.\" — the approved template for moved deliveries, taking params {site, day}. render(template_id, params) raises KeyError for unknown templates and ValueError if the filled text exceeds MAX_LENGTH = 140.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage is the only way to send a text. It raises RuntimeError if feature(\"sms_enabled\") is off, ValueError if household.sms_ok is False, renders the template, assigns id via format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], \"SMS-\")), and appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl (IRREVERSIBLE — nothing ever removes or edits a line). notify_rerouted must call this once per eligible household to guarantee exactly one text each.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "registry/register.py provides load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household]; with active_only=True it filters to status == \"active\". get_household(household_id) raises KeyError for unknown ids. Household fields include site (distribution site the household collects from), sms_ok (agreed to receive SMS, default True), status (\"active\"|\"inactive\"|\"merged\"), and phone.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "distribution/planner.py build_plan(today=None) currently calls best_route(warehouse, hh.site, network) per active household and sets delivery.route_id/delivery.vehicle from the result, else marks delivery.status = \"unreachable\". It imports from logistics.routes: best_route, sites_served, trips_needed, and from logistics.access: load_network. Deliveries are dataclass Delivery with fields household_id, warehouse_id, site, sku, kits, route_id, vehicle, status (\"planned\"|\"unreachable\").", "file": "distribution/planner.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "sites_served(warehouse_id, network=None) -> list[str] returns sorted unique r['to'] sites for routes from the warehouse — a ready-made pattern for producing name-ordered site lists, which rerouted_sites must also return (list[str] in name order).", "file": "logistics/routes.py"}, {"id": "R11", "statement": "core/ids.py next_number(existing_ids, prefix: str) -> int returns 1 + the highest number used so far with the prefix; queue_sms uses it with prefix \"SMS-\" for new message ids, so notify_rerouted does not need to manage ids itself.", "file": "core/ids.py"}]}}
